arfimapping.description: OpenRecon Bloch-Siegert B1 mapping from reconstructed magnitude and phase image messages. The runtime implements the workflow from `Read_7T_all_rev_openRecon.m`: detects 1Tx versus 8Tx from the frame count, uses the revised four-echo calculation, dedicated transmit-phase frames, and pre/post reference frames, builds an optional QC magnitude mask, converts phase counts to radians, corrects the scanner DICOM BSp polarity, computes BSp, measured B1, phase, and B0, then sends selected maps as explicit MRD volume images. Default outputs are B1, BSp, Tx phase, and B0 maps. Enable `sendmask` to also return the computed QC mask. The default phase scaling is the MATLAB DICOM conversion `phase * 2*pi/4096 - pi`. Every complete, nonconstant 3D output volume is mapped to scanner pixels spanning `0..4095`; DICOM rescaling and image comments record the inverse mapping back to physical units. B1 is reported in uT, BSp and Tx phase in degrees, B0 in Hz, and the mask as binary. Small negative BSp values are retained in the phase output and clamped only in the separate nonnegative copy used for the B1 square-root calculation. OpenRecon runtime notes: `recipes/blochsiegertb1mapping/OpenReconREADME.md`. Build and validate:

arfirecon.description: OpenRecon ARFI magnitude and phase reconstruction. Every magnitude and phase frame is returned as a multi-slice 2D series with source geometry and slice positions preserved. Single Freq divides one-based frames into sequential groups of `ARFI Block Length`. Odd groups form the noFUS set and even groups form the withFUS set. Multiple Freq uses `myTemp = floor((sqrt(floor((frame_number-1)/2)*8+1)+1)/2)` and assigns a frame to withFUS when `frame_number > myTemp * myTemp`. The runtime forms complex data as `magnitude * exp(i * phase)`, averages the withFUS and noFUS sets independently, and outputs `angle(withFUS_average * conj(noFUS_average))` as `<source> ARFI phase`. Magnitude and wrapped phase frames are also returned in `<source> Magnitude` and `<source> Phase` series. When `Send Phase Standard Deviation` is enabled, every complex frame is multiplied by the conjugate of its set's complex mean. The sample standard deviation of the residual phase is output separately as `<source> withFUS phase standard deviation` and `<source> noFUS phase standard deviation`. A one-frame set produces zero. Phase outputs are converted to degrees. Nonconstant volumes use DICOM pixels `0..4095`, with `RescaleSlope` and `RescaleIntercept` recording the mapping back to physical values. Outputs use `Keep_image_geometry = 1` and are sent as one 2D image per slice with the matching source position. `ARFI Schemes` defaults to Single Freq, `ARFI Block Length` defaults to 25, and `Send Phase Standard Deviation` defaults to disabled. The runtime does not calculate B1, Bloch-Siegert phase, B0, or a mask. OpenRecon runtime notes: `recipes/arfirecon/OpenReconREADME.md`. Build and validate:

blochsiegertb1mapping.description: OpenRecon Bloch-Siegert B1 mapping from reconstructed magnitude and phase image messages. The runtime implements the workflow from `Read_7T_all_rev_openRecon.m`: detects 1Tx versus 8Tx from the frame count, uses the revised four-echo calculation, dedicated transmit-phase frames, and pre/post reference frames, builds phase and magnitude masks, converts phase counts to radians, corrects the scanner DICOM BSp polarity, computes BSp, measured B1, phase, and B0, then sends selected maps as explicit MRD volume images. B1 and B0 maps are always returned. BSp and Tx phase remain configurable, and the computed masks are never returned. When Apply Mask is enabled, the MATLAB-derived magnitude mask is applied to every returned map. Mask holes are filled slice by slice and then across the 3D volume. BS phase/B1 and B0 are filtered with a polynomial fit (order 20 for 1Tx, order 10 for 8Tx) and Gaussian sigma 0.5; Apply Filter changes BS phase from untrusted-only replacement to whole-volume replacement. The default phase scaling is the MATLAB DICOM conversion `phase * 2*pi/4096 - pi`. Every complete, nonconstant 3D output volume is mapped to scanner pixels spanning `0..4095`; DICOM rescaling and image comments record the inverse mapping back to physical units. B1 is reported in uT, BSp and Tx phase in degrees, and B0 in Hz. For 1Tx, a reference-amplitude map in V is also returned using `11.74 * ABS_Tx_Ref_Amp / B1`. Processing-information histogram images are generated for masked B1 (one per Tx channel) and masked B0; they use uT and Hz source units respectively. Small negative BSp values are retained in the phase output and clamped only in the separate nonnegative copy used for the B1 square-root calculation. braid.description: BRAID: Brain Age Identification from Diffusion MRI BRAID estimates brain age from diffusion MRI. Unlike its counterparts, which typically use anatomical features (such as volume and shape of brain regions) to assist in the estimation, BRAID deliberately destroys anatomical information. Through non-rigid transformations, BRAID minimizes anatomical information to better focus on subtle microstructural changes that predate apparent anatomical changes in neurodegeneration.

dafne.description: Dafne is a program for the segmentation of medical images, specifically MR images, that includes advanced deep learning models for an automatic segmentation. The user has the option of refining the automated results, and the software will learn from the improvements and modify its internal models accordingly. In order to continuously improve the performance, the deep learning modules are stored in a central server location. Dafne uses incremental learning and federated learning to continuously adapt the models to the need of our users. This means that when you perform a segmentation, initially it will not be perfect. You will then have the chance to refine it. When you are satisfied with your dataset, you will export your ROI masks (see below). During this export procedure, the software automatically learns from your refined segmentation and sends the updated model back to our servers. This is why the export procedure takes some time. We will automatically integrate your updated model with the models of our other users, so you will always receive the most accurate predictor. You can also manually perform the incremental learning from the Tools menu (see below)

the segmentation sub-pipeline (seg) employs advanced deep learning networks for fast, accurate segmentation and volumetric calculation of the whole brain and selected substructures.

lesionquantificationtoolkit.description:
LQT is an R implementation of the lesion quantification toolkit, based on the paper “Lesion Quantification Toolkit: A MATLAB software tool for estimating grey matter damage and white matter disconnections in patients with focal brain lesions” by Griffis et al. The LQT is “a publicly available software package for quantifying the structural impacts of focal brain lesions. It uses atlas-based approaches to estimate parcel-level grey matter lesion loads and multiple measures of white matter disconnection severity that include tract-level disconnection measures, voxel-wise disconnection maps, and parcel-wise disconnection matrices. The toolkit also estimates lesion-induced increases in the lengths of the shortest structural paths between parcel pairs, which provide information about changes in higher-order structural network topology.”

The R package creates data structures necessary for applying the methods directly to MNI-registered lesion maps from either a single patient or a full study. The package then allows the user to create figures for visualization and summary, and to compile analysis-ready datasets for research.

openreconi2iexample.description: Minimal OpenRecon image-to-image reference. Receives reconstructed MRD image messages and sends outputs according to the enabled output options. The scanner label defaults enable original pass-through, inversion, and segmentation. Inversion is also the runtime default when no parameter payload is provided. Enable `sendoriginal` to pass the original 2D image stream through on `image_series_index = 100`. Inverted magnitude images are returned as `<source>-inverted` on `image_series_index = 99`; disable `invert` to omit them. Enable `segment` to extract the brightest foreground object and send `<source>-segment` outputs starting on `image_series_index = 101`. Segment output handling is controlled by `segmentheadergeometry`: `explicit_volume_derived_header` sends segmentation as an explicit derived volume, `3d_series_segment_header` sends 3D source-geometry masks with segmentation header identity, `2d_segment_header` sends 2D source-geometry masks with segmentation header identity, `2d_segment_header_originals` sends the same masks without scanner postprocessing child-role metadata, `2d_derived_image_header` sends 2D source-geometry masks with derived image header identity, and `2d_source_image_header` sends 2D source-geometry masks with source image header identity. When originals and segments are both enabled, originals are sent first and segment outputs are sent after them. Multi-contrast inputs with repeated slice positions are split into one segmentation output per source volume group. Enable `segmentationcolormap` with `segment` to add `MicroDeltaHotMetal.pal` LUT metadata to segmentation outputs. Enable `upsampled` to send one double-slice-count `<source>-upsampled` volume on `image_series_index = 102`. Enable `sendreformatsagittal` or `sendreformatcoronal` to send explicit sagittal/coronal 3D reformat volumes of the segment data starting on `image_series_index = 121`. Enable `sendcomputedmip` to send one `<source>-mip` maximum intensity projection image on `image_series_index = 103`. Enable `sendmetrics` to send segmented-region volume in image comments and a `<source>-metrics` DICOM image table on `image_series_index = 120`. The metrics table is sent as a standalone explicit derived output so scanner inline postprocessing does not attach to it. The rendered pixels are pre-oriented for scanner display and use standalone identity geometry instead of inheriting scan orientation. Original copies are normally sent first as source-native 2D images with `Keep_image_geometry = 1`. The pass-through keeps the source protocol, sequence, image-type, MiniHead, and slice metadata as intact as possible while assigning new returned-series UIDs. Returned originals use a one-based per-series `image_index`. Meta and MiniHead storage counters are restamped from the returned stream so `NumberInSeries`, `ChronSliceNo`, and `SliceNo` remain consistent with the MRD header; valid source partition counters are preserved for multi-partition inputs such as wholebody Dixon. If a source group cannot be sent safely as a 2D stream, the job fails before send rather than packing the originals, because scanner MIP/MPR postprocessing depends on the original stream. When `sendoriginal` is paired with `segmentheadergeometry = explicit_volume_derived_header`, the returned originals are sorted by projected physical slice position so their frame order matches the returned explicit segment volume. With `segmentheadergeometry = explicit_volume_derived_header`, segmentation outputs are sent as one explicit derived volume per source group with `Keep_image_geometry = 0`, `DataRole = Image`, and `SegmentExplicitVolume = 1`. These outputs are batched separately from originals. With `segmentheadergeometry = 3d_series_segment_header`, segmentation outputs are sent as one returned 3D-derived series per source group with one MRD image per source slice. The slices use `Keep_image_geometry = 1`, `DataRole = Segmentation`, `SegmentSourceGeometry = 1`, `SegmentOutputGeometry = 3d`, unique returned `slice` / `image_index` counters, source physical positions, and restamped Meta and MiniHead storage fields. With `segmentheadergeometry = 2d_segment_header`, masks keep source physical geometry, use `Keep_image_geometry = 1`, `DataRole = Segmentation`, `SegmentSourceGeometry = 1`, and the explicit segmentation `ImageType`. With `segmentheadergeometry = 2d_segment_header_originals`, masks use the same source-geometry segmentation header identity, but do not set `SegmentPostProcessingChildRole` or restamp `ExamDataRole` on the segment stream so scanner postprocessing can remain on the original stream. With `segmentheadergeometry = 2d_derived_image_header`, masks use the same source-geometry 2D header path but keep `DataRole = Image` and use a derived segment `ImageType`. With `segmentheadergeometry = 2d_source_image_header`, masks use the same source-geometry 2D header path but keep `DataRole = Image` and source `ImageType`, `DicomImageType`, and `ImageTypeValue4` identity. Segment reformats are packed explicit 3D volumes with centered slab geometry, `Keep_image_geometry = 0`, no `IceMiniHead`, `image_index = 1`, `slice = 0`, and matching `slice_count`, `NumberOfSlices`, and `ImagesInAcquisition`. When originals and segments are both enabled, segment outputs are sent after original outputs in a separate MRD image message. Returned outputs strip scanner `ImageTypeValue3` metadata and `IceMiniHead` `ImageTypeValue3` entries because some sequences reject that protocol field during OpenRecon conversion. Original pass-through preserves Dixon subtype identity. 2D source-image-header mask outputs preserve source identity, including Dixon subtype tokens. OpenRecon runtime notes and scanner option-combination tables: `recipes/openreconi2iexample/OpenReconREADME.md`. Scanner logs include an `openreconi2iexample runtime version=...` marker, `OPENRECONI2I_POSTPROCESSING target=...`, the independent segment controls in the configured-output line, and one `OPENRECONI2I_BATCH ...` marker before every MRD image send. The main reference for PALM is the same as for randomise:

* Winkler AM, Ridgway GR, Webster MA, Smith SM, Nichols TE. Permutation inference for the general linear model. NeuroImage, 2014;92:381-397 (Open Access)

For correction across contrasts (option -corrcon), the most detailed reference is:

* Alberton BAV, Nichols TE, Gamba HR, Winkler AM. Multiple testing correction over contrasts for brain imaging. Neuroimage. 2020 Mar 19:116760. (Open Access)

For Non-Parametric Combination (NPC; options -npc, -npcmod and -npccon), classical multivariate tests (MANOVA, MANCOVA; option -mv) assessed with permutations, and for correction over contrasts and/or modalities (options -corrcon and -corrmod), the reference is:

* Winkler AM, Webster MA, Brooks JC, Tracey I, Smith SM, Nichols TE. Non-Parametric Combination and related permutation tests for neuroimaging. Hum Brain Map. 2016 Apr;37(4):1486-511. (Open Access)

For the multi-level exchangeability blocks (options -eb, -vg, and for HCP data), the reference is:

* Winkler AM, Webster MA, Vidaurre D, Nichols TE, Smith SM. Multi-level block permutation. Neuroimage. 2015;123:253-68. (Open Access)

For the accelerated permutation inference (options -accel or -approx), the reference is:

* Winkler AM, Ridgway GR, Douaud G, Nichols TE, Smith SM. Faster permutation inference in brain imaging. Neuroimage. 2016 Jun 7;141:502-516. (Open Access)

For additional theory of permutation tests in neuroimaging, please see and cite:

* Nichols TE, Holmes AP. Nonparametric permutation tests for functional neuroimaging: a primer with examples. Hum Brain Map. 2002 Jan;15(1):1-25.

* Holmes AP, Blair RC, Watson JD, Ford I. Nonparametric analysis of statistic images from functional mapping experiments. J Cereb Blood Flow Metab. 1996 Jan;16(1):7-22.
palm.description: PALM \u2014 Permutation Analysis of Linear Models \u2014 is a tool that allows inference using permutation methods, offering a number of features not available in other analysis software. These features currently include: Ability to work with volumetric and surface-based formats, including facewise data, as well as with non-imaging data; A range of various regression and permutation strategies; Statistics that are robust to heteroscedasticity; Shuffling of sets of observations, to allow, for instance, the analysis of certain designs with repeated measurements, with no missing data; Shuffling of observations with complex, tree-like covariance structure (such as for the Human Connectome Project); Permutation with sign-flipping (wild bootstrap); Modified Non-Parametric Combination (NPC) for joint inference over multiple modalities, or multiple contrasts, or both together, with various combining functions available; Classical multivariate statistics (MANOVA, MANCOVA) for joint inference over multiple modalities, assessed through robust permutation methods, and also parametrically when such approximations exist; Correction over multiple contrasts, multiple modalities, for images with or without the same size or geometry, including non-imaging data, controlling the FWER or FDR; Various acceleration methods based on the test statistics and their distributions.

synthseg.description: SynthSeg is a contrast- and resolution-agnostic brain MRI segmentation tool. This container packages `mri_synthseg` and the trained weights from FreeSurfer 8.2.0: SynthSeg 2.0 (default), SynthSeg 1.0 (`--v1`), SynthSeg-robust (`--robust`), the cortical parcellation and QC networks, and Photo-SynthSeg 1.0 (`--photo`).
